hero.headline: Global stocks fall as South Korean market plunges and Middle East tensions drive oil prices higher
hero.body:
Stock markets around the world fell on Monday as a technology sector selloff deepened and renewed hostilities between Iran and Israel sent oil prices climbing. The declines were particularly sharp in Asia, where South Korea's Kospi index dropped nearly 9 percent at one point, forcing trading to be briefly suspended.

The sharp decline in South Korean equities reflected a broader retreat from technology stocks. Foreign investors have sold billions of dollars worth of Korean stocks this year, with the latest selloff hitting major chip makers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix hard. Their share prices fell 9 percent and 6 percent respectively. The technology sector decline rippled across global markets, as investors reassessed valuations in artificial intelligence companies that had driven gains in recent months.

Markets in other Asian regions also registered significant losses. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 3 percent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng dropped 1.5 percent. European markets similarly declined, with the pan-European Stoxx 600 index falling nearly 0.9 percent. Chip manufacturers and technology firms were among the biggest losers, with companies like ASML falling 3.2 percent and Aixtron dropping almost 6 percent. Finland's Nokia fell 5 percent.

Investors have grown more nervous about the valuation of artificial intelligence stocks, particularly as interest rate concerns mount. Tech companies at the forefront of the AI boom are seeking substantial funding to finance massive capital expenditure plans. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said "markets are now pricing in a greater likelihood of an interest rate rise from the Federal Reserve this year."

"Fears of higher interest rates come just as tech giants are seeking fresh funding to help finance eye-watering capital expenditure plans," she said. "There is concern that assets being invested in today could become obsolete further down the road."

Oil prices jumped nearly 5 percent after Iran and Israel exchanged direct strikes over the weekend. Brent crude rose to $97.60 a barrel, up from $93 a barrel the previous week. The escalation in hostilities has heightened concerns about potential disruptions to oil supplies from the region, particularly raising fears that the conflict could prevent the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping channel through which approximately one-fifth of the world's oil and gas supply normally flows.

The combination of the technology sector retreat and Middle East tensions created a risk-off environment across global financial markets. U.S. stock futures pointed to a lower opening on Wall Street, continuing downward momentum from Asian and European trading sessions. The declines followed a steep selloff in tech stocks the previous week, when the tech-heavy Nasdaq index lost nearly 5 percent of its value and the S&P 500 dropped 2 percent on a weekly basis, ending nine weeks of gains.

cards.headline: Trump calls for immediate halt to Israel-Iran fighting as ceasefire unravels
cards.teaser: President Trump urged Israel and Iran to immediately stop shooting on Monday after renewed military strikes threatened to collapse the April ceasefire between t.
cards.body:
President Trump urged Israel and Iran to stop shooting "immediately" on Monday as military hostilities resumed between the two nations. The escalation began Sunday when Iran launched missiles at Israel, marking the first direct Iranian attack since a ceasefire took effect in early April. Israel responded with strikes on Tehran and other Iranian cities.

The renewed fighting threatens to unravel months of fragile peace and complicates diplomatic efforts. Iran's decision to directly intervene on behalf of its proxy Hezbollah represents a significant shift from the proxy-based conflicts that characterized the regional tension since spring. The BBC's international editor warned the public has reason to worry, noting the consequences of the war will be felt for generations.

cards.headline: Weight loss drug maker loses quarter of market value after safety data raises investor concerns
cards.teaser: Shares of Zealand Pharma sank 25 percent following new clinical data on an obesity treatment developed with Boehringer Ingelheim.
cards.body:
Zealand Pharma's stock price fell sharply after a study revealed that nearly one in five patients discontinued the company's obesity shot survodutide due to side effects. The drug, developed in partnership with Boehringer Ingelheim, is being evaluated in phase 3 trials.

The new safety data showed side effects significant enough to prompt patient withdrawals, though company executives maintained the drug's tolerability profile remains consistent with others in its class. The treatment had previously shown promise in reducing visceral and liver fat. The market reaction underscores investor sensitivity to safety profiles in the competitive weight loss drug sector.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Congo spreading at unprecedented rate, officials say
cards.teaser: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than previous outbreaks, according to health officials.
cards.body:
The Democratic Republic of Congo is experiencing an Ebola outbreak that is spreading at an unprecedented pace, according to the Africa CDC and other health officials. The rapid transmission of the virus represents a significant escalation of the public health crisis in the central African nation.

The speed at which Ebola is spreading is raising serious concerns about the ability of health workers and international agencies to effectively contain the epidemic.

cards.headline: Republicans prepare third budget bill before midterm elections
cards.teaser: GOP leaders are assembling another party-line spending package ahead of the August recess to advance Trump agenda items before voters head to the polls.
cards.body:
Republican leadership is working to pass a third budget reconciliation bill before Congress breaks for its month-long August recess. The effort represents the party's final opportunity to enact major portions of President Trump's legislative priorities through the party-line budget process before the midterm elections potentially shift control of Congress.

The tight timeline creates pressure on Republicans to resolve internal disagreements and assemble a package that can pass both chambers. Party leaders face the challenge of balancing competing priorities within the caucus while maintaining enough support to pass legislation without Democratic votes.

cards.headline: House to vote on immigration enforcement funding and surveillance powers
cards.teaser: Congress faces a packed week with votes scheduled on a $69.5 billion border security package and extension of warrantless spying authority.
cards.body:
The House is preparing to vote on a budget reconciliation package that would provide $69.5 billion in funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol operations. The legislation represents a key component of the Republican immigration enforcement agenda and will move through the party-line reconciliation process.

Lawmakers also plan to address a long-term extension of the government's warrantless surveillance powers under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The dual priorities create a legislative crunch as Republicans work to advance both measures before the August recess.

cards.headline: Armenian Prime Minister Claims Election Victory in Test of Russian Influence
cards.teaser: Nikol Pashinyan's pro-Western party secured nearly 50% of the vote in an election seen as pivotal for Armenia's geopolitical orientation.
cards.body:
Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's Civil Contract Party secured nearly 50 percent of the vote in a parliamentary election, according to results announced Monday. The victory positions Pashinyan's pro-Western government to continue leading the country.

The election was widely viewed as a referendum on Armenia's geopolitical direction. Pashinyan's party comfortably beat other contenders in the race, which observers characterized as a test of Russian influence in the former Soviet nation.

hero.headline: Earthquake and Landslide Kill at Least 32 in Southern Philippines
hero.teaser: A 7.8-magnitude earthquake struck off Mindanao, triggering a deadly landslide and widespread destruction.
hero.body:
A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck off Mindanao in the southern Philippines on Monday, killing at least 32 people and injuring more than 200 others. The powerful quake collapsed buildings across the region and triggered a deadly landslide. Tens of thousands of residents were displaced from their homes.

The earthquake generated a 3-foot tsunami that reached nearby coasts in the Philippines, Indonesia, and Japan. Authorities warned residents to avoid damaged buildings due to the threat of aftershocks as rescue teams searched through debris in affected areas.

cards.headline: Armenian Prime Minister Claims Election Victory in Test of Russian Influence
cards.teaser: Nikol Pashinyan's pro-Western party secured nearly 50% of the vote in an election seen as pivotal for Armenia's geopolitical orientation.
cards.body:
Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's Civil Contract Party secured nearly 50 percent of the vote in a parliamentary election, according to results announced Monday. The victory positions Pashinyan's pro-Western government to continue leading the country.

The election was widely viewed as a referendum on Armenia's geopolitical direction. Pashinyan's party comfortably beat other contenders in the race, which observers characterized as a test of Russian influence in the former Soviet nation.

cards.headline: Malawi Evacuates Citizens From South Africa Amid Xenophobic Violence
cards.teaser: Malawi joined several African nations transporting their citizens out of South Africa following reports of attacks on migrants.
cards.body:
Malawi is repatriating its citizens from South Africa as xenophobic violence against migrants intensifies. The country joins several other African nations in transporting their nationals out amid growing safety concerns.

The backlash has been fueled by recent protests and campaigns calling for illegal immigrants to leave. African migrants report living in extreme fear, noting that even legal status provides little protection as anti-immigration sentiment spreads across the country.

cards.headline: Pope and Spanish Prime Minister Meet, United in Opposition to Trump
cards.teaser: Pope Leo XIV and Pedro Sánchez, who have both clashed with President Trump, held talks on Monday.
cards.body:
Pope Leo XIV met with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez on Monday, bringing together two leaders who have recently clashed with President Trump. The Pope, leader of the Catholic Church, and Sánchez, an atheist, find themselves on the same side despite their vastly different worldviews.

Both leaders have publicly opposed Trump administration policies in recent weeks, though their motivations may differ. The meeting highlights a broader international pushback against certain American policies under the Trump administration. The unusual alliance between the religious leader and the secular prime minister underscores the breadth of European concerns about current US policy directions.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall as Middle East Conflict Resumes
cards.teaser: Markets in Europe and Asia dropped on renewed attacks between Iran and Israel, while oil prices rose.
cards.body:
Stock markets in Europe and Asia fell on Monday following a sharp decline in US technology stocks the previous week. The sell-off was driven by investor concerns about major artificial intelligence companies and their ability to fund substantial spending plans. Oil prices rose as Iran and Israel exchanged military strikes, renewing worries about potential disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz.

The dual pressures of weakness in the technology sector and Middle East geopolitical tensions combined to create downward pressure across global stock indexes.

cards.headline: Extreme Heat Poses Ongoing Threat in Pakistani District
cards.teaser: Residents of Dadu District face temperatures reaching 125 degrees amid sandstorms, drought, and flooding.
cards.body:
People in Dadu District, Pakistan, are struggling with extreme heat as temperatures reach 125 degrees Fahrenheit. The area faces multiple climate challenges throughout the year, including sandstorms, drought, and flooding, with each season bringing new hardships for residents.

The extreme temperatures force residents to seek shade and adjust their daily routines to survive the heat. Dadu District's vulnerability to multiple climate threats illustrates the compounding challenges facing communities in regions experiencing severe weather extremes. The high temperatures pose health risks and make ordinary activities dangerous during peak heat hours.

cards.headline: Israel Targets Iranian Petrochemical Complex in Mahshahr
cards.teaser: The facility produces materials Iran says are for civilian use but that Israel argues have military applications.
cards.body:
Israel struck the Mahshahr petrochemical complex in Iran as part of its retaliatory attacks on Monday. The facility manufactures materials that Iran maintains are intended for civilian purposes, but Israel contends the products are also used in military applications.

The targeting of the petrochemical complex represents an escalation beyond purely military sites. Mahshahr is a significant industrial facility in Iran's petrochemical sector. The strike raises questions about the scope of targets Israel considers legitimate in its conflict with Iran and whether industrial infrastructure will remain in the crosshairs if hostilities continue.

hero.headline: Remote workers report higher isolation and anxiety than office counterparts, study finds
hero.body:
People working remotely experience greater social isolation, anxiety, and sadness compared to those not in remote positions, according to new research released Monday. The findings add complexity to the ongoing debate over workplace arrangements as companies and employees navigate post-pandemic work models.

The study examined the mental health and social well-being of workers in remote positions versus those working in traditional office settings or hybrid arrangements. Researchers found measurably higher rates of negative mental health outcomes among those working exclusively from home, challenging the popular narrative that remote work universally improves quality of life.

Despite these findings, researchers emphasized that mandating a full return to office environments is not the appropriate solution. The study suggests that while remote work creates certain challenges around connection and mental health, forcing employees back into offices fails to address the underlying issues and ignores the legitimate benefits that flexible work arrangements provide to many people.

The research arrives as many American companies continue to refine their workplace policies. Some major employers have implemented return-to-office mandates, while others have embraced permanent remote or hybrid models. The findings suggest that organizations need more nuanced approaches that address the social and mental health needs of remote workers rather than simply eliminating remote work options.

The study points to a tension between employee preference and employee well-being. While surveys consistently show that many workers prefer remote arrangements for reasons including commute elimination and schedule flexibility, the research indicates these benefits may come with hidden costs to mental health and social connection that warrant attention from both employers and employees.

cards.headline: Earthquake kills at least 32 in southern Philippines
cards.teaser: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck the southern Philippines, triggering small tsunami waves across the region.
cards.body:
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck the southern Philippines on Monday, killing at least 32 people and injuring more than 200 others. The offshore quake caused widespread building collapses across the affected region. Authorities warned residents to avoid damaged structures due to the risk of aftershocks.

The earthquake generated a 3-foot tsunami that reached nearby coasts in the Philippines, Indonesia, and Japan. Rescue and recovery efforts were underway in the earthquake zone as emergency responders worked to assist those affected by the disaster.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Congo spreading at unprecedented rate, officials say
cards.teaser: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than previous outbreaks, according to health officials.
cards.body:
The Democratic Republic of Congo is experiencing an Ebola outbreak that is spreading at an unprecedented pace, according to the Africa CDC and other health officials. The rapid transmission of the virus represents a significant escalation of the public health crisis in the central African nation.

The speed at which Ebola is spreading is raising serious concerns about the ability of health workers and international agencies to effectively contain the epidemic.

cards.headline: Former USAID official discusses agency operations in new book
cards.teaser: Nicholas Enrich, who served at USAID under four administrations, has written a book about his experiences as a whistleblower.
cards.body:
Nicholas Enrich, who worked at the U.S. Agency for International Aid across four presidential administrations, has published a book titled Into the Woodchipper: A Whistleblower's Account of How the Trump Administration Shredded USAID. In the book, Enrich describes his experiences at the federal agency responsible for international development and humanitarian assistance.

Enrich discusses the agency's role in global health response, including its work on the Ebola crisis, and reflects on the changes he observed within the organization during his tenure under multiple administrations.

cards.headline: Pope calls for moral renewal in address to Spanish parliament
cards.teaser: The pope addressed Spain's legislature for the first time, urging lawmakers to ensure respect for human dignity.
cards.body:
In a historic first, the pope addressed the Spanish legislature and called for "moral renewal" in both government and public life. He stressed that lawmakers must work to uphold the inherent dignity of all people.

The speech underscores the Vatican's engagement with the Spanish government on matters of ethics and governance.

cards.headline: Red state, blue state divide driven by factors beyond politics, research shows
cards.teaser: New research suggests ideological sorting involves multiple factors including taxes and safety, not just political alignment.
cards.body:
Recent research challenges the assumption that Americans sort into red and blue states primarily based on political ideology. The study reveals that ideological sorting is more nuanced, with people weighing multiple considerations when choosing where to live.

Tax policies and safety concerns rank alongside political climate as significant factors influencing relocation decisions. This suggests that geographic political polarization stems from a combination of overlapping motivations rather than politics alone.

cards.headline: Starmer asks Apple and Google to block nude images on children's phones
cards.teaser: The British prime minister called on tech companies to activate features preventing children from accessing sexually explicit images.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Starmer has given Apple and Google a September deadline to install software that blocks explicit images on children's phones. The companies must activate nudity-detection algorithms or other technical solutions to prevent minors from taking or sharing sexually explicit photos, unless verified as adults.

If the tech firms fail to implement these safeguards by the deadline, the government will introduce legislation to enforce the requirement. Starmer is pushing both companies to use existing technical capabilities to protect children from exposure to explicit content on their devices.

cards.headline: Roche agrees to $2.3 billion drug development deal with Nurix Therapeutics
cards.teaser: The pharmaceutical giant is partnering with Nurix on a pill targeting blood cancers, multiple sclerosis, and chronic hives.
cards.body:
Roche entered a $2.3 billion agreement with Nurix Therapeutics to develop a BTK degrader drug currently in late-phase trials. The deal includes $700 million in upfront payments, with the medication targeting blood cancer conditions as well as multiple sclerosis and hives.

The partnership positions Roche to compete directly with other pharmaceutical companies developing similar treatments. BTK degraders represent a newer approach to treating these conditions compared to traditional inhibitor drugs. The late-phase status of Nurix's candidate suggests the therapy could reach market relatively quickly if trials prove successful.

cards.headline: European economic recovery stalls as Middle East conflict persists
cards.teaser: Analysts point to an extended period of elevated prices and reduced growth rather than a short-term shock.
cards.body:
Europe's economic recovery is faltering as escalating attacks between Iran and Israel create fresh uncertainty. Stock markets in Europe and Asia have declined, driven by a technology sector selloff and rising oil prices triggered by the Middle East conflict. Economists warn that the situation points to prolonged inflation and slower growth rather than a temporary disruption.

The geopolitical instability is adding pressure to energy costs and supply chains across European markets. Central banks and governments face mounting challenges as they attempt to support economic growth amid persistent inflation and market volatility stemming from the ongoing conflict.

cards.headline: Artificial intelligence tool helps doctors with clinical diagnosis and treatment decisions
cards.teaser: OpenEvidence, a rapidly growing startup, uses AI to assist physicians in finding answers to medical questions.
cards.body:
A startup called OpenEvidence has developed an artificial intelligence system designed to help doctors locate clinical information for diagnosing patients and determining treatment plans. The platform aims to provide physicians with evidence-based answers to medical questions more efficiently.

The company has experienced rapid growth as healthcare providers seek technological tools to support clinical decision-making. The AI system draws on medical literature and clinical data to assist doctors in their diagnostic work. The technology represents a growing trend of AI applications in healthcare settings, where time-sensitive decisions require quick access to relevant medical information.

cards.headline: Marks & Spencer creates 1,000 traineeships for young people
cards.teaser: The British retailer launched a program aimed at addressing youth unemployment and lack of job training opportunities.
cards.body:
Marks & Spencer has launched a new traineeship scheme for 1,000 young people. The initiative is designed to address the "growing challenge" of young people who are not in employment, education, or training.

The program aims to provide these individuals with practical experience and support as they enter the workforce, helping to tackle barriers they may face in finding employment opportunities.

cards.headline: UK government pressures Apple and Google to block explicit content on children's devices
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Starmer called on tech companies to activate built-in features preventing children from accessing sexually explicit images.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Keir Starmer has given Apple and Google until September to activate software that blocks sexually explicit images on children's phones and tablets. The technology must either detect and prevent the creation or sharing of nude images, or restrict access to such content unless users are verified as adults.

Starmer warned that if the companies fail to implement these measures by the deadline, the government will introduce legislation to enforce the requirement. Both firms have existing nudity-detection algorithms and parental control features available in their operating systems that could be activated for this purpose.

hero.headline: Astronomers identify source of repeating cosmic radio signals
hero.body:
Astronomers have identified the source of mysterious repeating radio signals from space, describing the discovery as a breakthrough in understanding these cosmic phenomena. The signals originate from an accreting white dwarf binary system, according to research published in Nature. The identification came through work by a student astronomer who traced the periodic radio and X-ray emissions to their source.

White dwarf binaries consist of a dense stellar remnant pulling matter from a companion star. As material from the companion star spirals onto the white dwarf, the process generates intense radiation across multiple wavelengths. The periodic nature of both radio and X-ray emissions from this system provides scientists with a way to study the mechanics of these interactions in unprecedented detail.

Researchers at UNC-Chapel Hill contributed to cracking the cosmic radio mystery. The signals had puzzled astronomers because of their regular timing and distinctive characteristics. Unlike random cosmic noise, these emissions arrived in predictable patterns that suggested a structured physical process rather than chance events.

The discovery gives astronomers what researchers call a Rosetta stone for understanding similar signals detected elsewhere in space. By linking the radio emissions to a known type of stellar system, scientists can now develop models to explain other mysterious signals that share similar characteristics. The white dwarf binary system provides a laboratory for studying how matter behaves under extreme gravitational and magnetic conditions.

The findings have implications for how astronomers search for and interpret signals from deep space. Rather than requiring exotic explanations, some repeating radio signals can now be understood as natural byproducts of stellar evolution and interaction. The research demonstrates how identifying even one source can illuminate entire classes of cosmic phenomena, giving scientists tools to decode signals that previously defied explanation.

cards.headline: Apple hosts annual developer conference with focus on artificial intelligence
cards.teaser: Apple holds its WWDC 2026 event with expectations centered on improvements to Siri and broader AI capabilities.
cards.body:
Apple is hosting its annual Worldwide Developers Conference with attention focused on the company's artificial intelligence strategy. After two years of setbacks in AI development, the event represents another attempt to demonstrate progress in competing with other tech companies. The conference includes presentations on iOS 27 and updates across Apple's software platforms.

Investors are watching for announcements about AI features that could drive the next phase of growth for the company. The event comes as Apple works to overhaul Siri and integrate more sophisticated AI capabilities across its products. Tim Cook and other executives are expected to detail the company's approach to personal AI and how it will be implemented in future software releases.

cards.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft introduce new processors for AI-capable personal computers
cards.teaser: The two companies unveiled new hardware aimed at bringing artificial intelligence processing directly to consumer laptops.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced the RTX Spark processor, which the company describes as its most efficient PC chip. The announcement came at Computex alongside Microsoft's demonstration of the Surface Laptop Ultra, both designed to run AI applications locally rather than relying on cloud computing. Nvidia also introduced laptop chips as part of its strategy to expand AI processing beyond data centers.

The push represents a bet that consumer demand will grow for AI features that run directly on personal computers. Microsoft demonstrated the Surface Laptop Ultra to show how the new hardware enables AI capabilities in Windows PCs. The companies are working to establish AI-capable personal computers as a new category, though demand beyond specialized users remains unproven according to industry analysts.

cards.headline: Diver records rare footage of great white shark in Mediterranean Sea
cards.teaser: A volunteer diver captured video of an endangered great white shark between Tunisia and Sicily.
cards.body:
A volunteer diver encountered an endangered great white shark in waters between Tunisia and Sicily, capturing rare footage of the encounter. The diver described shaking as he filmed the endangered species in its natural habitat.

Great white shark sightings in the Mediterranean Sea remain uncommon, making this documentation a significant capture of the rarely seen animal in the region.

cards.headline: Uber opens interest list for Wayve robotaxi service in London
cards.teaser: UK Uber customers can now register interest in using self-driving vehicles from Wayve as the company expands autonomous ride options.
cards.body:
Uber has opened an interest list for UK customers to sign up for rides in Wayve robotaxis, with those who join receiving priority matching when the service launches later this year. The move marks a significant milestone for Uber in one of its largest markets.

The partnership reflects intensifying competition in London's autonomous vehicle sector, where Wayve and Waymo are both pursuing robotaxi services. By integrating Wayve's self-driving technology with its existing ride-hailing platform, Uber aims to establish an early foothold in the robotaxi market while giving the UK-based autonomous driving company access to a large customer base.

cards.headline: Axiom Space and Prada advance spacesuit design for NASA moon missions
cards.teaser: NASA astronauts on the Artemis IV mission will wear spacesuits developed in partnership with the Italian fashion house.
cards.body:
Axiom Space and Prada have revealed new details about the Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment (LCVG), a specialized base layer astronauts will wear beneath their spacesuits during the Artemis IV mission to the Moon in 2028. The high-tech undergarment is designed to regulate temperature and maintain comfort in the lunar environment.

The collaboration between the aerospace company and Italian luxury brand combines engineering expertise with fashion design innovation. The LCVG represents a critical component of the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU) spacesuit system being developed for NASA's lunar missions.

cards.headline: Atlus announces Persona 6 at Xbox Games Showcase
cards.teaser: The video game developer revealed the next installment in the Persona series featuring a graveyard aesthetic and green color scheme.
cards.body:
Atlus confirmed Persona 6 during the Xbox Games Showcase 2026, ending months of speculation surrounding the long-running RPG series. The announcement came with a brief teaser that gave fans their first official look at the upcoming title.

The reveal followed leaks that had circulated online earlier, with Sega taking action to remove the leaked images before the planned announcement. Persona 6 marks the return of the series and continues a strong showing for Japanese RPGs at this year's gaming events.

hero.headline: Nelly Korda wins first US Women's Open by one stroke over Charley Hull
hero.body:
World number one Nelly Kord captured her first US Women's Open title on Sunday, holding off England's Charley Hull and Gaby Lopez by a single stroke in a dramatic finish. The victory marks her second consecutive major championship and her fourth major title overall.

Kord completed the final round with a steady two-under 69, but the win came down to a tense moment on the 18th green. Her second putt from just over two feet caught the edge of the cup and rolled halfway around the circumference before dropping in. The dramatic conclusion gave her the one-shot victory over Hull, who was seeking her first major championship.

The American's ability to close out a competitive field under pressure demonstrates the form that has carried her to the world number one ranking. Despite entering the final round as the betting favorite, Kord maintained her composure throughout the closing holes to hold off her challengers and secure the most prestigious title in American women's golf.

Hull's runner-up finish represents her best result at the US Women's Open to date. The English golfer, who has established herself as one of Europe's leading players, continues to pursue her first major championship victory. Her narrow defeat at this event exemplifies the competitive international fields that have increasingly featured at the tournament in recent years.

Kord claimed the $2.5 million first prize for her victory. The US Women's Open holds special significance as the oldest of women's golf's five major championships. The tournament rotates among premier American courses and consistently attracts the strongest fields in women's golf. Winning the event provides automatic entry into the tournament for the next decade and secures a player's place in the sport's history.

The victory comes at a significant moment in women's professional golf. American players have dominated the sport's major championships in recent years, and Kord's win continues that trend. Her success demonstrates her ability to perform in high-pressure situations, a quality essential for winning major championships.

With three additional major championships remaining on the calendar, Kord's victory provides momentum as the golf season progresses. Her back-to-back major titles mark a period of sustained excellence that has elevated her to the top ranking in women's golf. The dramatic manner of her triumph on the 18th green will likely be remembered as one of the defining moments of her career, showcasing both her skill and her mental strength under pressure.

cards.headline: Jose Mourinho set to become Real Madrid head coach after Perez re-election
cards.teaser: Jose Mourinho is expected to be confirmed as Real Madrid's new head coach following Florentino Perez's re-election as club president.
cards.body:
Florentino Perez has been re-elected as Real Madrid president until 2030, securing an overwhelming victory in the club's first contested election in 20 years. Perez polled 65% of the vote against challenger Enrique Riquelme, who received 35% in a ballot that drew 33,555 members.

With Perez's position secured, Jose Mourinho will now be confirmed as the club's new head coach. Perez's re-election also paves the way for his plans to sell 5% of the club.

cards.headline: Charles Leclerc calls Ferrari brake failure in Monaco crash borderline dangerous
cards.teaser: Charles Leclerc criticized Ferrari after a brake failure caused him to crash out of the Monaco Grand Prix while running in a podium position.
cards.body:
Charles Leclerc described his Ferrari's brake failure as "borderline dangerous" after crashing out of the Monaco Grand Prix. Running in a podium position late in the race, three of his four brakes failed as he approached a corner, causing him to lose control and hit the barriers.

The mechanical issue ended what had been a promising race for Leclerc on his home circuit. The incident raises concerns about the reliability of Ferrari's braking system during competitive racing conditions.

cards.headline: Thomas Tuchel says Jude Bellingham faces fight for England starting spot at World Cup
cards.teaser: England manager Thomas Tuchel said midfielder Jude Bellingham will have to compete for a place in the starting lineup at the World Cup.
cards.body:
Jude Bellingham will have to compete for a starting position in England's midfield at the World Cup, according to manager Thomas Tuchel. Despite his important role at club level, the midfielder is not assured a place in the team's lineup for the tournament.

Tuchel's comments highlight the quality of England's midfield options as the team prepares for the World Cup. Bellingham will need to perform well in training and any remaining warm-up matches to earn his spot in the starting eleven.

cards.headline: Christian Eriksen conscious and expected to leave hospital after on-field collapse
cards.teaser: Denmark midfielder Christian Eriksen is in good spirits and expected to be discharged from hospital soon after collapsing during a match against Ukraine.
cards.body:
Christian Eriksen is conscious and in good spirits following his collapse during Denmark's friendly match against Ukraine on Sunday, according to Denmark's national team doctor Morten Boesen. The midfielder is expected to be discharged from hospital soon.

Eriksen collapsed during the 65th minute at Odense Stadium while holding his chest. Medical staff attended to him immediately and the match was abandoned. He was transported to hospital where he underwent tests and observation.

cards.headline: England coach McCullum backs captain Stokes to regain batting form
cards.teaser: England head coach Brendon McCullum expressed confidence that captain Ben Stokes will soon return to his best batting form.
cards.body:
England captain Ben Stokes' batting is "not too far away" from a return to form, according to head coach Brendon McCullum. The coach's backing comes as Stokes continues to lead the team through a challenging period with the bat.

McCullum has praised his players for moving past their Ashes disappointment in Australia, hailing their bravery following England's Test win over New Zealand at Lord's. The coach acknowledged the difficult batting conditions but expressed satisfaction with how his team maintained their attacking approach despite low scores.

cards.headline: British hitting partner reveals role in Serena Williams comeback secret
cards.teaser: A British hitting partner for Serena Williams disclosed how he became involved in keeping her tennis comeback plans confidential.
cards.body:
British tennis player David Quayle traveled to Florida to work as a hitting partner for Serena Williams as she prepared for her return to competitive tennis. Quayle, from Wigan, was brought in to help her get match-ready while keeping her comeback plans under wraps.

Williams' training team maintained strict confidentiality around her preparations ahead of her return to the tour at Queen's. Quayle's account to BBC Sport offers a rare glimpse into the behind-the-scenes work required for one of tennis's greatest players to make a comeback.

hero.headline: Qween Jean Becomes First Openly Trans Person to Win Tony Award
hero.body:
Costume designer Qween Jean achieved a historic milestone at the Tony Awards, becoming the first openly transgender person to receive the prestigious theater honor. Jean won the award for her costume design work on the musical Cats.

During her acceptance speech, Jean reflected on the current state of society. "The world right now is deeply, deeply combating so many ailments, and we know as a society that when we come together, we can make real, permanent change," she stated from the stage. The win represents a significant moment for Broadway and for LGBTQ+ visibility at major entertainment awards ceremonies.

Jean's victory comes as the Tony Awards continue to recognize broader diversity within the theater industry. Her win demonstrates the growing acknowledgment of talent from communities that have historically been underrepresented in major entertainment honors and on Broadway stages.

The Tony Awards ceremony itself celebrated numerous achievements across multiple categories. A theatrical revival of Arthur Miller's classic play Death of a Salesman emerged as the evening's biggest winner, taking home six awards total. The production's success highlighted the continued resonance of classic American theater with modern audiences.

Acting honors were distributed among several performers, with John Lithgow and Lesley Manville among the night's winners in their respective categories. These awards recognized the strongest performances across Broadway productions from the season.

Beyond award presentations, the ceremony featured musical performances from various artists. The performances showcased the range of entertainment that Broadway offers to audiences each year.

Jean's historic achievement adds to a broader pattern of change within major entertainment institutions. The Tony Awards have increasingly worked to expand recognition across the industry, acknowledging excellence from previously marginalized communities. This shift reflects larger conversations about representation and inclusion in theater and entertainment generally.

The Tony Awards remain one of the most important recognition ceremonies in American theater. Held annually, the ceremony honors outstanding work in Broadway productions and has become a major cultural event that draws significant attention to the theater industry.

Jean's win serves as a marker of progress for transgender representation in mainstream entertainment. While the entertainment industry has made strides in recent years toward greater inclusion, major award wins by openly transgender individuals remain notable achievements. Her presence on the Tony Awards stage and her recognition for her artistic work contributes to ongoing visibility and normalization of transgender professionals in theater and beyond.

The recognition Jean received underscores how the Broadway community continues to evolve in its acknowledgment of diverse talent and perspectives. As the industry expands its recognition of creators from all backgrounds, achievements like Jean's become part of the broader narrative of change within American theater.

cards.headline: Arthur Miller Revival Death of a Salesman Takes Six Tony Awards
cards.teaser: The revival of the Arthur Miller classic led the night with six total awards at the Tony ceremony.
cards.body:
A revival of Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman dominated the 2026 Tony Awards, winning six awards and emerging as the night's most decorated production. The classic American drama was recognized across multiple categories, underscoring Broadway's continued appetite for reimagined canonical works.

John Lithgow and Lesley Manville were among the leading acting winners at the ceremony, both earning recognition for their performances in the production.

cards.headline: Grammy-Winning Musician Mark Oraybibi Killed
cards.teaser: The artist known professionally as Stormzy was remembered by fellow musicians following his death.
cards.body:
Grammy-winning musician Mark Oraybibi died, prompting tributes from fellow artists in the music industry. Rapper Wretch 32 described Oraybibi as "a gem" in his remembrance.

Stormzy was among the stars who shared memories of the late musician. Oraybibi had achieved recognition in the music industry, earning a Grammy Award during his career.

cards.headline: Idris Elba Says James Bond Casting Rumors Were Never Realistic
cards.teaser: The actor addressed long-running speculation about taking over the 007 role after Daniel Craig's departure.
cards.body:
Idris Elba has dismissed years of speculation about him taking on the James Bond role, calling the rumors "never legit" and "not realistic." The 53-year-old actor addressed the persistent reports in a new cover interview, explaining that audiences wouldn't accept a Black male actor in the iconic part.

Elba, known for his work in heroic roles, has been linked to the Bond succession since Daniel Craig's 2021 departure. With his current focus on Masters of the Universe alongside Nicholas Galitzine, the actor has now definitively closed the door on the long-running casting conversation.

cards.headline: Money Heist Producer Sonia Martinez Joins El Estudio
cards.teaser: The television executive behind Money Heist and Locked Up has been appointed director of contents for the Spanish production company.
cards.body:
Sonia Martinez, the television executive behind Money Heist and Locked Up, has joined El Estudio as director of contents for Spain. The appointment aims to expand the production company's growth in the Spanish market.

El Estudio, established in 2020, operates offices in Madrid and Mexico City. The company is headed by Pablo Cruz. Martinez's track record on two of Spain's most successful recent television series positions her to lead content development at the production house.

cards.headline: Hugh Laurie Defends House Against Same Narrative Criticism
cards.teaser: The actor responded to viral criticism that the medical drama followed repetitive storylines during its eight-season run.
cards.body:
Hugh Laurie defended House against criticism that the medical drama relied on repetitive narrative structures. The English actor, who played the titular character on the Fox series from 2004 to 2012, responded to viral social media comments dismissing the show's format.

Laurie pushed back forcefully against reductive takes of the series. "If all you see is hospital, medical blah blah, then it wasn't meant for you," he said. The actor remains a passionate advocate for the show more than a decade after its conclusion, resisting characterizations that reduce it to procedural medical elements alone.

cards.headline: Maggie Gyllenhaal and Jesse Eisenberg to Receive Karlovy Vary Honors
cards.teaser: The actress and actor will be recognized at the 60th edition of the Czech Republic film festival in July.
cards.body:
The Karlovy Vary International Film Festival will honor Maggie Gyllenhaal and Jesse Eisenberg at its 60th edition, running July 3-11. Both are recognized for their work as actors, directors, and screenwriters.

Artistic director Karel Och said Gyllenhaal and Eisenberg "are distinguished by a certain trans-Atlantic sensitivity." He noted that their work as actors and directors demonstrates particular qualities that warranted recognition at the Czech festival.

hero.headline: Republicans prepare third budget bill before midterm elections
hero.teaser: GOP leaders are assembling another party-line spending package ahead of the August recess to advance Trump agenda items before voters head to the polls.
hero.body:
Republican leadership is working to pass a third budget reconciliation bill before Congress breaks for its month-long August recess. The effort represents the party's final opportunity to enact major portions of President Trump's legislative priorities through the party-line budget process before the midterm elections potentially shift control of Congress.

The tight timeline creates pressure on Republicans to resolve internal disagreements and assemble a package that can pass both chambers. Party leaders face the challenge of balancing competing priorities within the caucus while maintaining enough support to pass legislation without Democratic votes.

cards.headline: Trump calls for immediate halt to Israel-Iran fighting as ceasefire unravels
cards.teaser: President Trump urged Israel and Iran to immediately stop shooting on Monday after renewed military strikes threatened to collapse the April ceasefire between t.
cards.body:
President Trump urged Israel and Iran to stop shooting "immediately" on Monday as military hostilities resumed between the two nations. The escalation began Sunday when Iran launched missiles at Israel, marking the first direct Iranian attack since a ceasefire took effect in early April. Israel responded with strikes on Tehran and other Iranian cities.

The renewed fighting threatens to unravel months of fragile peace and complicates diplomatic efforts. Iran's decision to directly intervene on behalf of its proxy Hezbollah represents a significant shift from the proxy-based conflicts that characterized the regional tension since spring. The BBC's international editor warned the public has reason to worry, noting the consequences of the war will be felt for generations.

cards.headline: House to vote on immigration enforcement funding and surveillance powers
cards.teaser: Congress faces a packed week with votes scheduled on a $69.5 billion border security package and extension of warrantless spying authority.
cards.body:
The House is preparing to vote on a budget reconciliation package that would provide $69.5 billion in funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol operations. The legislation represents a key component of the Republican immigration enforcement agenda and will move through the party-line reconciliation process.

Lawmakers also plan to address a long-term extension of the government's warrantless surveillance powers under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The dual priorities create a legislative crunch as Republicans work to advance both measures before the August recess.

cards.headline: Tensions rise between Trump and congressional Republicans on policy disputes
cards.teaser: GOP lawmakers are increasingly speaking out against administration positions on multiple issues despite Trump's success in defeating defiant party members.
cards.body:
Growing numbers of Republican senators and House members are publicly breaking with President Trump on policy matters ahead of the midterm elections. The disagreements span multiple issues and come as members face pressure from constituents in their home districts and states.

The tension persists despite Trump's track record of successfully backing primary challengers against Republican incumbents who opposed him. Members are becoming more willing to voice dissent even as the president maintains strong influence over the party base and has demonstrated ability to reshape congressional membership through endorsements.

cards.headline: House Freedom Caucus faces membership shake-up as prominent members leave
cards.teaser: Six Freedom Caucus members are departing Congress, setting up changes in the conservative group's leadership and relationship with Trump.
cards.body:
The House Freedom Caucus will undergo significant changes next year as six of its high-profile members leave Congress. The departures will reshape the conservative group's membership and likely affect its dynamics with Republican leadership and the White House.

The members are leaving to pursue higher office rather than seeking reelection to the House. The turnover creates opportunities for new members to join the caucus and potentially shift its tactical approach and policy priorities in the next Congress.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Interior Secretary secured the Democratic nomination and could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. The victory positions her as the party's nominee in the general election this fall.

Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States if she wins in November. She previously served as a U.S. Representative from New Mexico before joining the Biden cabinet.

cards.headline: Southern states implement new district maps, disrupting election preparations
cards.teaser: Last-minute redistricting in several states is forcing election officials, candidates, and voters to adjust to redrawn congressional boundaries.
cards.body:
Multiple Southern states are implementing new congressional district maps just months before the November elections, creating confusion for election administrators and voters. The Supreme Court cleared the way for Louisiana and Alabama to use new maps after its April decision that weakened provisions of the Voting Rights Act.

The late changes have forced candidates to reassess their races and caused uncertainty about which voters belong in which districts. Election officials are working to update voter registration systems and communicate the changes to residents before early voting begins.
